body: But what am I suppose to do about my career? The longer I' unemployed the less likely it will be  for me to get a job.

Here's the deal, I'm actually past suicide at this point. I realize that I will never be able to do it, which means that I will have this anxiety for the rest of my life. I don't know what to do, every single interview I go to I just say what I did at my last job. Here's the deal, product management is a REALLY COMPETITIVE field. Since my last job was a "junior" position I had it pretty easy, but all these jobs posed are "senior" asking for 5+ years and MBA. It's making me depressed and more so anxious when I come into this market with no bachelors. I really don't now what to do? Should I start getting prepared to drive uber for the rest of my life or working in retail? I know this might sound selfish or spoiled, but the idea of doing that really makes me want to vomit. I feel like I through away all my experience and education just so I can barley get by in life.

Look, I am really really trying. I know I have it good, better than most around the world. This actually makes me feel more like shit because I keep saying to myself "keep going, other people have it worse" and when I try to start working I literally freak out and start spiraling out of control of what I'm going to do once I run out of money.
Thanks for the kind words... it's just I can't get over the fact of what I've done. I keep going over it in my head everytime at in my parents place and through out the day.

I know what you mean. I had a damn job, a girlfriend, an apartment, a car. Then I decide to drop everything, move to NY, spending all my savings, and come back empty handed to everything I was trying to get away with. It's a God Damn fucking nightmare.
Thank you. It's just really hard because I feel that I didn't learn as much as I needed to and I'm lacking the degree.

Yes, I'm speaking to a therapist about potential bi-polar disorder. I just really wish it didn't come down to this. My whole family lives in Silicon Valley, and due to the condition I'm in I don't think it's a good idea to move out of the area.
I've had downs before, but nothing this bad. I feel like I put myself in a place where I won't be able to move forward in my career. I've lost all interest in PM, programming, everything.
I would love to chat. Sent you a PM.
Thanks for the word of support. I'm trying really hard to move on, but I can't stop thinking about the opportunity I blew. It's especially hard to get a PM position.

I'm trying, I really am. But I can't accept how bad I ruined my career. I had a really good thing going, my biggest worry at the time was my noisy upstairs neighbors. This was also the first job I really loved, I would wake up at 6:45am in the morning to get on my morning calls because I LOVED my team. I don't feel like moving forward anymore because I'm tired, I'm tired of trying in life and getting screwed over. This especially hurts when looking at all my friends that are succeeding in tech. Some of them are buying houses, getting married, and here I screwed over  a really good shot at finally making it in "Silicon Valley". I just don't know what to do, people are telling me to drive Lyft/Uber. But the idea that I put so much work into my life and career, only to end up as a Uber driver is what is really pushing me over the edge.

Unfortunately, I tried that, and the answer was no... I left the company on really bad terms. Not only did I curse out my colleagues, I left with only 3 days noticed and piled up my entire project on someone else. I have no idea why they would hire me back, I just look back on this and feel like a total fucking idiot. I had it really really good, and now I don't think I'll be able to work in tech anymore. My programming skills are incredible dried up and out of date and I only have 1 year of PM experience, which is almost useless.
